title: Making a Mine Speak
paras: An environmental exhibition begins not with a spectacular specimen but with a disputed stream. For a display about an abandoned sulphur mine, curator Nara first assembles the documentary [[paraphernalia|paraphernalia]] of extraction: drainage maps, laboratory notebooks and stained inspection cards. She must [[peruse|peruse]] these alongside workers’ accounts, distinguishing measured contamination from recollections of an unexplained [[malaise|malaise]] that once unsettled the neighbouring village.

The exhibition’s central object is then constructed: a transparent channel through which water passes over sealed replicas of fractured rock. Actual [[pyrite|pyrite]], whose oxidation can generate acidic drainage, remains in a separate dry case. A magnified photograph of an [[alga|alga]] collected downstream introduces the biological evidence; its caption explains why a single organism cannot establish the condition of an entire watercourse.

To give this chemistry a human chronology, Nara [[intersperse|intersperses]] photographs of sampling sites among reproductions of administrative records. One training booklet invokes [[leninism|Leninism]] to justify party leadership over industrial production; another document records the official [[exoneration|exoneration]] of a technician accused of falsifying water tests. Neither is presented as an explanation sufficient, by itself, to account for the stream’s deterioration.

Finally, the labels are tested with visitors, whose questions expose ambiguities invisible to their authors. Nara’s patient [[disposition|disposition]] proves useful when a retired miner objects to the arrangement: she adjusts the sequence without suppressing uncomfortable evidence. Such revisions may [[redound|redound]] to the museum’s credit, but their immediate purpose is more exacting: to make a damaged landscape intelligible without manufacturing a conveniently innocent past.
zh: 一场环境展览的起点并非一件引人注目的标本，而是一条存在争议的溪流。为了筹备关于一座废弃硫矿的展览，策展人娜拉首先搜集与开采有关的整套文书资料：排水图、实验室记录本，以及污渍斑斑的检查卡。她必须将这些资料与工人的叙述对照细读，区分实测的污染情况与人们的回忆；后者讲述的是一种原因不明、曾令邻村人心不安的身体不适。
随后，展览的核心展品开始制作：一条透明水槽，水从封有保护层的碎裂岩石模型上流过。真正的黄铁矿仍放在另一个干燥的展柜中；这种矿物氧化时可能产生酸性排水。一张在下游采集的藻类的放大照片引出了生物学证据；图片说明解释了为什么仅凭一个生物个体，无法判定整条水道的状况。
为了给这些化学过程补上人类活动的时间线，娜拉将采样点的照片穿插在行政档案的复制件之间。一本培训手册援引列宁主义，为党领导工业生产提供理论依据；另一份文件则记载，一名曾被指控伪造水质检测结果的技术员获得了官方无罪认定。展览并未将其中任何一份材料当作足以单独解释溪流恶化的依据。
最后，展品说明交由参观者试读，他们提出的问题暴露出撰写者未曾察觉的歧义。一位退休矿工对展品编排提出异议时，娜拉耐心的性格发挥了作用：她调整了顺序，却没有隐去令人不安的证据。这类修改或许有助于提升博物馆的声誉，但其直接目的更为严格：让人们理解一片遭到破坏的土地，同时不编造一个仿佛无人有责的过去。

q.s: Nara obtained the laboratory notebooks from former mine workers.
q.why: 文章列出记录本，但未说明其提供者。

q.s: The genuine pyrite is kept separately from the channel carrying water.
q.why: 水槽内为岩石模型，黄铁矿另置干燥展柜。

q.s: Nara removed uncomfortable evidence when revising the display sequence.
q.why: 末段明确说她调整顺序但未隐去证据。
